stances.claim: President Ramos deserves profound gratitude for appointing CJ to the SC despite his being 'thoroughly unworthy' -- a selfless act of discernment that launched CJ's highest judicial career.
stances.rhetorical_move: selfless-discernment tribute to appointing president (humility marker throughout)

stances.claim: President Arroyo's manner of appointing CJ as Chief Justice -- without prior interview, surprising him completely -- was an act of quiet confidence that overwhelmed CJ with gratitude, sending him to bended-knee prayer.

Despite the Panganiban Court ruling against some Arroyo initiatives, their post-retirement friendship -- sustained through cordial Malacañang visits and her presence at the 80th birthday celebration -- demonstrates that judicial independence and personal respect are not mutually exclusive.

notable_anecdotes: Ramos's 'Dear Tiger Chief Justice Art' salutation -- and CJ's self-deprecating response: 'Perhaps, what he really meant is that I am a harmless and toothless tiger' -- the most affectionate single exchange in any of CJ's tribute columns.

The scene of CJ being informed of his CJ appointment by a paper slip during a speech in a five-star hotel ballroom -- freezing at the rostrum, going to the car with Leni, and praying on bended knees at their parish church -- the most vivid and cinematic moment in CJ's personal columns.

Dr. Frank Laubach's 'Life begins at 80' essay: at 80 everyone helps carry your bags, you have a perfect excuse for everything, people are surprised you're still alive -- 'So, please, folks, try to make it to 80. It's the best time of life.'

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban shares edited closing remarks from his December 20 'Ageless Passion' 80th birthday musicale (produced by Donna May Lina, directed by Bart Guingona, featuring 18 original Ryan Cayabyab songs with lyrics by Jeff Agustin) as his Christmas Day column, thanking two presidents. He thanks President Ramos, who 'plucked me from anonymity' and recently sent his book '2030 One World, One Community, One Family' with the salutation 'Dear Tiger Chief Justice Art' -- which CJ joyfully receives, adding self-deprecatingly that Ramos probably meant 'a harmless and toothless tiger.' He quotes Ramos's letter ('life begins at 40, so at 80 one is born again'), adapts Reinhold Niebuhr's Serenity Prayer for age 80 with comic effect, and shares Dr. Frank Laubach's essay 'Life Begins at 80' -- concluding: 'So, please, folks, try to make it to 80. It's the best time of life.' He thanks President Arroyo, who appointed him Chief Justice without prior interview -- the vacancy occurring December 20, 2005, and CJ learning of it the next day from a paper slip while delivering a speech in a five-star hotel ballroom. He froze at the rostrum, descended the stage, went to his car with Leni, drove to their parish church, and 'on bended knees, fervently thanked the Lord for His bountiful blessings.' Despite the Panganiban Court's defeat of some Arroyo initiatives, she remained cordial and occasionally invited CJ to Malacañang after retirement -- and her presence at the December 20 celebration affirmed that they remain 'friends and firm believers in the vitality of our democracy, the supremacy of the rule of law, and the wisdom of checks and balances.'
